Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Santosh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 516 of 2023, under Sections 376, 504, 506 of I.P.C., Police Station - Sahjanawan, District - Gorakhpur, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case. He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.

The FIR was instituted regarding the outraging the modesty of the daughter of the Umesh Sahni vs State Of U.P. on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131431951/
1 informant but the allegations of rape have been escalated in the statement of the victim recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. and that too after due deliberations and legal consultations.
5.

entities.text: Umesh Sahni vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.11.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6.

Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

7. In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785, this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant- Umesh Sahni, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./ 351BNSS

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the Umesh Sahni vs State Of U.P. on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131431951/
2 witnesses.
